A sample of n=49n=49n=49 observations is taken from a normal population with a standard deviation of σ=10\sigma=10σ=10. Sample mean is Xˉ=55\bar{X}=55Xˉ=55.

99 percent Confidence Interval \textbf{99 percent Confidence Interval }99 percent Confidence Interval 

For a 99 percent level of confidence, the value of zzz is obtained by locating 0.99/2=0.49500.99/2=0.49500.99/2=0.4950 in the table given in Appendix B1. The value of z=2.58z=2.58z=2.58.

Xˉ±zσn=55±2.58×1049=55±2.58×107=55±3.69\begin{align*} \bar{X} \pm z\frac{\sigma}{\sqrt{n}}&=55 \pm 2.58 \times \frac{10}{\sqrt{49}}\\ &=55 \pm 2.58 \times \frac{10}{7}\\ &=55 \pm 3.69 \end{align*} Xˉ±zn​σ​​=55±2.58×49​10​=55±2.58×710​=55±3.69​

So, X1=55−3.69=51.31X_1 =55-3.69=51.31X1​=55−3.69=51.31 and X2=55+3.69=58.69X_2=55+3.69=58.69X2​=55+3.69=58.69. So, 999999 percent confidence interval for population mean is (51.31,58.69)(51.31, 58.69)(51.31,58.69).

🎯 Result

(51.31,58.69)(51.31, 58.69) (51.31,58.69)

A sample of n=250n=250n=250 observations is taken from a normal population with a standard deviation of σ=25\sigma=25σ=25. Sample mean is Xˉ=20\bar{X}=20Xˉ=20.

a. Standard error of the mean\textbf{a. Standard error of the mean} a. Standard error of the mean

σXˉ=σ/n=25/250=25/15.81=1.58\begin{align*} \sigma_{\bar{X}}&=\sigma/ \sqrt{n}\\ &=25 / \sqrt{250}\\ &=25/15.81\\ &=1.58\\ \end{align*} σXˉ​​=σ/n​=25/250​=25/15.81=1.58​

b. \textbf{b. }b. The central limit theorem says that the sampling distribution of the mean becomes a normal distribution as sample size increases. A sample of 250 observations is large enough to assume that the sampling distribution will follow the normal distribution.

c. 95 percent Confidence Interval \textbf{c. 95 percent Confidence Interval }c. 95 percent Confidence Interval 

For a 95 percent level of confidence, the value of zzz is obtained by locating 0.95/2=0.47500.95/2=0.47500.95/2=0.4750 in the table given in Appendix B1. The value of z=1.96z=1.96z=1.96.

Xˉ±zσn=20±1.96×25250=20±1.96×1.58=20±3.097\begin{align*} \bar{X} \pm z\frac{\sigma}{\sqrt{n}}&=20 \pm 1.96 \times \frac{25}{\sqrt{250}}\\ &=20 \pm 1.96 \times 1.58\\ &=20 \pm 3.097 \end{align*} Xˉ±zn​σ​​=20±1.96×250​25​=20±1.96×1.58=20±3.097​

So, X1=20−3.097=16.903X_1 =20-3.097=16.903X1​=20−3.097=16.903 and X2=20+3.097=23.097X_2=20+3.097=23.097X2​=20+3.097=23.097. So, 959595 percent confidence interval for population mean is (16.903,23.097)(16.903, 23.097)(16.903,23.097).

🎯 Result

a. 1.581.581.58

c. (16.903,23.097)(16.903, 23.097)(16.903,23.097)

A sample of n=49n=49n=49 steady smokers is taken from a normal population with a standard deviation of σ=$5\sigma=\$5σ=$5. Sample mean is Xˉ=$20\bar{X}=\$20Xˉ=$20.

a. Point estimate of the population mean \textbf{a. Point estimate of the population mean }a. Point estimate of the population mean 

The sample mean of $20\$20$20 is a point estimate of the unknown population mean and is the best estimate, given the data.

b. 95 percent Confidence Interval \textbf{b. 95 percent Confidence Interval }b. 95 percent Confidence Interval 

For a 95 percent level of confidence, the value of zzz is obtained by locating 0.95/2=0.47500.95/2=0.47500.95/2=0.4750 in the table given in Appendix B1. The value of z=1.96z=1.96z=1.96.

Xˉ±zσn=20±1.96×549=20±1.96×57=20±1.4\begin{align*} \bar{X} \pm z\frac{\sigma}{\sqrt{n}}&=20 \pm 1.96 \times \frac{5}{\sqrt{49}}\\ &=20 \pm 1.96 \times \frac{5}{7}\\ &=20 \pm 1.4 \end{align*} Xˉ±zn​σ​​=20±1.96×49​5​=20±1.96×75​=20±1.4​

So, X1=20−1.4=18.6X_1 =20-1.4=18.6X1​=20−1.4=18.6 and X2=20+1.4=21.4X_2=20+1.4=21.4X2​=20+1.4=21.4. So, 959595 percent confidence interval for population mean is ($18.6,$21.4)(\$18.6, \$21.4)($18.6,$21.4).

Interpretation\textbf{Interpretation}Interpretation: About 95 percent of these confidence intervals are expected to contain the population mean μ\muμ i.e mean amount steady smokers spend on cigarettes.

Chapter 9

Exercise 7

Page 306
PROBLEM STATEMENT
Chapter 9, Page 306
💡 Solution A
Step 1

In finding the point estimate of a given problem, we need to recall the definition of a point estimate. Point estimate is the estimation for the population parameter and it can be represented by the sample mean. Since the population standard deviation is known, we will use the confidence interval formula when σ\sigmaσ is known:

x‾±zσn\overline{x}\pm z\dfrac{\sigma}{\sqrt{n}} x±zn​σ​

to find the interval from which population mean falls. In addition, we will be using the z−z-z−table. Based on the obtain interval, we can discuss the estimated mean number of gallons of gasoline sold to Bob's customers.

Step 2

(a) Point Estimate of the Population Mean:

Here, we determine a statistic that will be our estimate for the population parameter. The point estimate will be the sample mean of the data. Since the sample mean of the number of gallons sold to the customers is 8.608.608.60 gallons, then the point estimate of the unknown population mean will also be 8.60 gallons\boxed{8.60\text{ gallons}}8.60 gallons​.

Step 3

(b) 99%\boldsymbol{99\%}99% Confidence Interval:

To find the confidence interval with 99%99\%99% confidence level, we are going to use the formula for the confidence interval for a population mean with σ\sigmaσ known:

x‾±zσn\overline{x}\pm z\dfrac{\sigma}{\sqrt{n}} x±zn​σ​

Where x‾\overline{x}x is the sample mean, zzz is the z−z-z−statistic from zzz table, σ\sigmaσ is the standard deviation of the population, and nnn is the total number of samples.

Now, let us find the values of the quantities involved in the formula. Based on the problem, the mean number of gallons sold is 8.608.608.60. Thus,

x‾=8.60\color{#ff9c8c}{\overline{x}=8.60} x=8.60

The confidence level that we are going to use is 99%99\%99%. Dividing the confidence level by 222 then locating the obtained value into the z−z-z−table we have:

0.99÷2=0.49500.99\div2=0.4950 0.99÷2=0.4950

Then we locate 0.49500.49500.4950 on the z−z-z−table. 0.49500.49500.4950 or its closest equivalent is found on row 2.52.52.5 and column 0.080.080.08. The z−z-z−statistic that corresponds to 0.49510.49510.4951 is will be the sum of the row and column values thus,

z=2.5+0.08=2.58z=2.5+0.08=\color{#ff9c8c}{2.58} z=2.5+0.08=2.58

Step 4

Then, the population standard deviation is known and that is:

σ=2.30\color{#ff9c8c}{\sigma=2.30} σ=2.30

while the number of samples is

n=60\color{#ff9c8c}{n=60} n=60

Substituting the values into the confidence interval formula then simplifying we obtain:

x‾±zσn=8.60±(2.58)(2.3060)(Write the formula.)=8.60±(2.58)(2.307.746)(Evaluate the square root.)=8.60±(2.58)(0.297)(Divide.)=8.60±0.766(Multiply.)\begin{aligned} \overline{x}\pm z\dfrac{\sigma}{\sqrt{n}}&=8.60\pm (2.58)\left(\dfrac{2.30}{\sqrt{60}}\right)&&(\text{Write the formula.})\\[0.8em] &=8.60\pm (2.58)\left(\dfrac{2.30}{7.746}\right)&&(\text{Evaluate the square root.})\\[0.8em] &=8.60\pm (2.58)(0.297)&&(\text{Divide.})\\[0.8em] &=8.60\pm 0.766&&(\text{Multiply.})\\[0.8em] \end{aligned}x±zn​σ​​=8.60±(2.58)(60​2.30​)=8.60±(2.58)(7.7462.30​)=8.60±(2.58)(0.297)=8.60±0.766​​(Write the formula.)(Evaluate the square root.)(Divide.)(Multiply.)​

Thus, the confidence interval limits are:

8.60−0.766=7.834       and       8.60+0.766=9.3668.60-0.766=7.834\ \ \ \ \ \ \text{ and }\ \ \ \ \ \ 8.60+0.766=9.366 8.60−0.766=7.834       and       8.60+0.766=9.366

Therefore, the 99%99\%99% confidence interval for the population mean is

7.834 to 9.366\boxed{7.834\text{ to }9.366} 7.834 to 9.366​

Step 5

(c) Interpretation:

From (b), we calculated the 99%99\%99% confidence interval for the population mean which is 7.834 to 9.3667.834\text{ to }9.3667.834 to 9.366. This interval indicates that the mean number of gallons of gasoline sold to Bob's customers falls within 7.834 to 9.3667.834\text{ to }9.3667.834 to 9.366 gallons with 99%99\%99% confidence level. Observe also that the point estimate for the population mean which is 8.608.608.60 falls into the interval.

💡 Solution A
Step 1

$\textbf{a. Sample size n=15n=15n=15 and level of confidence is 959595 percent}$

For a 959595 percent confidence interval and degrees of freedom df=n−1=15−1=14df=n-1=15-1=14df=n−1=15−1=14, ttt value is 2.1452.1452.145.

Step 2

(b) If the sample size decreases, then we contain less information about the population and thus our estimates will be less accurate. If our estimates are less accurate, then our estimate is further from the true value of the population parameter and thus the confidence interval needs to be wider. However, a confidence interval is wider when the margin of error is increased and thus we can decrease the sample size by increasing the margin of error.

It is also possible to decrease the sample size by decreasing the coefficient coefficient.

For example, when we require a margin of error of 0.05 (instead of 0.01), then we obtain a sample size of n=228n=228n=228.

🎯 Result

(a) n=5683n=5683n=5683

(b) Decrease confidence coefficient or increase margin for error.
